title: feat(middleware): add Request Body Size Limit middleware (413 Payload Too Large)
text:
This adds an opt-in ASGI middleware to enforce a maximum HTTP request body size, returning 413 Payload Too Large when exceeded. The middleware pre-reads up to the configured limit, short-circuits on overflow, and includes unit tests verifying acceptance and rejection paths. This provides a first-class safety guard aligned with production needs without impacting existing apps unless enabled.

title: ⚡️ Optimize dependency graph flattening
text:
## Summary

Replace recursive dependency-graph flattening with an iterative preorder traversal.

The previous implementation constructed a flattened subtree at each dependency level and copied that subtree into every ancestor. It also used linear list membership when skipping repeated dependencies.

This change:

- accumulates dependencies directly into one flat result;
- uses set-backed repeated-dependency detection, while retaining compatibility with unhashable callables;
- replaces recursive

title: ⚡️ Optimize dependency graph flattening
⚡️ Optimize dependency graph flattening
text:
t dependency execution.

## Complexity

For a dependency chain of depth `d`, the previous recursive implementation repeatedly copied descendant lists into their ancestors, resulting in `O(d²)` work and memory references.

The iterative implementation traverses the dependency graph and accumulates the flattened result directly, making a chain `O(d)`.

For repeated dependencies, set-backed membership changes duplicate detection from `O(n²)` to average `O(n)` for hashable dependency cache keys. The

title: ⚡️ Optimize dependency graph flattening
text:
p changes duplicate detection from `O(n²)` to average `O(n)` for hashable dependency cache keys. The list fallback preserves support for unhashable callables.

## Internal representation

The root flattened `Dependant` retains the same preorder dependency sequence and combined parameter fields.

One internal detail changes: entries in the root flat dependency list no longer retain their own recursively flattened descendant lists. All descendants are accumulated directly in the root flat list. Ex

title: ⚡️ Optimize dependency graph flattening
text:
ively flattened descendant lists. All descendants are accumulated directly in the root flat list. Existing FastAPI consumers operate on the root flat collections.

## Benchmarks

A local synthetic benchmark flattening a 500-node dependency chain with `skip_repeats=True` measured:

| Implementation | Time |
|---|---:|
| `master` | ~7.8 ms |
| This PR | ~1.6 ms |

This is approximately a 4.9× improvement for that case.

The PR adds a focused CodSpeed benchmark so CI can provide the authoritative c

title: fix(sse): preserve empty data strings and trailing newlines in format_sse_event
text:
## Description
This PR resolves line-splitting issues in `format_sse_event()` in `fastapi/sse.py` by replacing `.splitlines()` with `.split('\n')`.

## Details
- Prevents empty data payload strings (`data_str=''`) or strings with trailing newlines from being stripped by `.splitlines()`.
- Complies strictly with the W3C SSE specification section 9.2.6.

title: fix(encoders): use errors='replace' when decoding bytes in jsonable_encoder
text:
## Description
This PR prevents `UnicodeDecodeError` crashes in `jsonable_encoder` by using `errors='replace'` when decoding `bytes` objects.

title: Fix SSE data payload dropping trailing newlines
text:
### Summary

`format_sse_event` splits the data payload with `str.splitlines()` before writing each `data:` field. This silently drops a **trailing** newline, so a `ServerSentEvent` whose data ends in `\n` is sent one field short and a client reconstructs the payload without its final newline.

`str.splitlines()` also treats characters as line breaks that the SSE wire format does **not** recognize (`\v`, `\f`, `\x1c`–`\x1e`, `\x85`, ` `, ` `), so those characters inside `raw_data` — documented a

title: Fix SSE data payload dropping trailing newlines
text:
(`\v`, `\f`, `\x1c`–`\x1e`, `\x85`, ` `, ` `), so those characters inside `raw_data` — documented as sent "as-is" — get wrongly split into separate `data:` fields.

### Reproduction

```python
from fastapi.sse import format_sse_event

format_sse_event(data_str="line1\n")
# actual:   b'data: line1\n\n'          -> client rebuilds "line1"  (trailing "\n" lost)
# expected: b'data: line1\ndata: \n\n'  -> client rebuilds "line1\n"

format_sse_event(data_str="a\x0bb")
# actual:   b'data: a\ndata: b\n

title: Fix SSE data payload dropping trailing newlines
text:
-> client rebuilds "line1
"

format_sse_event(data_str="a\x0bb")
# actual:   b'data: a
data: b

'     -> "\x0b" turned into a line break
# expected: b'data: a\x0bb

'         -> "\x0b" sent as-is
```

Per the [WHATWG event-stream format](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/server-sent-events.html#event-stream-interpretation), a stream is split into lines on **CR LF, CR, or LF only**, and a `data:` value is joined back with `
` on the client. To transmit `"line1
"` the server must em

title: Fix SSE data payload dropping trailing newlines
text:
d a `data:` value is joined back with `\n` on the client. To transmit `"line1\n"` the server must emit `data: line1` followed by an empty `data:` field.

### Fix

Split the payload on the SSE line terminators (`\r\n`, `\r`, `\n`) and keep the trailing empty field, instead of using `str.splitlines()`. Multi-line data, CR, and CRLF continue to encode exactly as before.

A unit test covering the trailing-newline, empty, multi-line, CR/CRLF, and non-SSE-separator cases is added. `fastapi/sse.py` sta

title: 🐛 Fix `exclude_defaults` not propagated to dict keys and values in `jsonable_encoder`
text:
## Problem

`jsonable_encoder` forwards `exclude_defaults` when recursing into list/tuple/set items, but drops it when recursing into dict keys and values — while the sibling flags `exclude_unset` and `exclude_none` *are* forwarded in that same dict branch. The same model with the same flag encodes differently depending on its container:

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel
from fastapi.encoders import jsonable_encoder

class M(BaseModel):
    a: int = 5

jsonable_encoder([M()], exclude_def

title: 🐛 Fix `exclude_defaults` not propagated to dict keys and values in `jsonable_encoder`
text:
ers import jsonable_encoder

class M(BaseModel):
    a: int = 5

jsonable_encoder([M()], exclude_defaults=True)       # [{}]
jsonable_encoder({"k": M()}, exclude_defaults=True)  # {"k": {"a": 5}}  <- flag silently ignored
```

Reproduced on 0.139.2.

## Fix

Forward `exclude_defaults` in the dict branch's key and value recursion, matching the list branch and the two sibling flags already passed there.

This deliberately does **not** change `include`/`exclude` propagation for dict values — that's

title: 🐛 Fix `exclude_defaults` not propagated to dict keys and values in `jsonable_encoder`
text:
ere.

This deliberately does **not** change `include`/`exclude` propagation for dict values — that's the broader design question tracked in discussion #15961; this PR only removes the inconsistency between the two container branches for a flag that is already documented as recursive.

## Tests

Added `test_encode_model_with_default_in_dict_and_list` covering list, dict, and dict-of-list nesting plus a guard that `exclude_unset`/`exclude_none` behaviour is unchanged.

`pytest tests/test_jsonable_

title: 🐛 Fix response_model_* params ignored for non-generator Iterable endpoints
text:
## Description

Fixes #15093

Non-generator endpoints with `Iterable[T]` return type had `response_model` set to `None` because `get_stream_item_type()` matched `Iterable` as a stream origin (it's in `_STREAM_ORIGINS`). This caused `serialize_response()` to fall back to `jsonable_encoder()`, ignoring `response_model_*` params like `exclude_none`, `exclude_unset`, and `exclude_defaults`.

## Changes

- **`fastapi/routing.py`**: Added `inspect.isasyncgenfunction/isgeneratorfunction` check before t

- **`tests/test_response_model_as_return_annotation.py`**: Added `test_iterable_return_type_response_model_inferred` verifying that `response_model_exclude_none` works for non-generator endpoints returning `Iterable[ItemOut]`

title: 🐛 Fix implicit path params with Starlette URL converters not recognized
text:
## Description

Fixes #14883

When using Starlette URL converters like `{param:int}` without an explicit `Path()` annotation, `get_path_param_names()` was returning the full converter pattern (e.g. `param:int`) instead of just the parameter name (`param`). This caused FastAPI to not recognize the parameter as a path parameter.

## Changes

- **`fastapi/utils.py`**: Updated `get_path_param_names()` to strip converter suffixes by splitting on `:`
- **`tests/test_starlette_urlconvertors.py`**: Adde

title: Optimize APIRoute handler caching and fix endpoint context cache
text:
## Summary

This PR fixes two issues in `routing.py`:

1. Cache the generated request handler for effective route contexts to avoid rebuilding it on every request.
2. Replace the `id()`-based endpoint context cache with a `WeakKeyDictionary` to avoid stale cache entries and allow unused entries to be garbage-collected.

## Motivation

While reviewing `routing.py`, I noticed that routes using an effective route context rebuild their request handler on every incoming request, even though

title: Optimize APIRoute handler caching and fix endpoint context cache
text:
ing an effective route context rebuild their request handler on every incoming request, even though the effective context itself is already cached and stable. Caching the generated ASGI application avoids repeating the same work and reduces unnecessary allocations.

I also noticed that `_endpoint_context_cache` is keyed by `id(func)`. Since object IDs may be reused after an object is garbage-collected, this can theoretically return stale endpoint metadata. Additionally, the cache never shrinks

title: Optimize APIRoute handler caching and fix endpoint context cache
text:
lected, this can theoretically return stale endpoint metadata. Additionally, the cache never shrinks because entries remain for the lifetime of the process. Using `WeakKeyDictionary` avoids both issues.

## Changes

- Added lazy caching of the generated ASGI application on `_EffectiveRouteContext`.
- Reused the cached application for subsequent requests.
- Replaced the `id()`-based endpoint context cache with `weakref.WeakKeyDictionary`.
- Added a fallback for callables that cannot be wea

title: Optimize APIRoute handler caching and fix endpoint context cache
text:
context cache with `weakref.WeakKeyDictionary`.
- Added a fallback for callables that cannot be weak-referenced by computing the context without caching.

## Expected Impact

- Reduces repeated request handler construction.
- Avoids unnecessary allocations on repeated requests.
- Eliminates potential stale cache lookups caused by `id()` reuse.
- Prevents unbounded growth of the endpoint context cache.
- Preserves existing behavior while improving efficiency.

## Related Discussion

## Testing

- Added tests covering the new behavior.
- Verified that the existing test suite passes.
- Confirmed that routing behavior remains unchanged while exercising the modified code paths.

title: Fix broken relative links in translated docs
text:
I noticed while looking at the translated documentation that there are three relative links that point to pages that are only in English. This results in 404s for users visiting the docs in any other locale than English.

What's broken
Affected files and links are:

docs//docs/deployment/versions.md — links to ../release-notes.md, which doesn't exist in any translated locale
docs//docs/help-fastapi.md — links to newsletter.md and fastapi-people.md#fastapi-experts, which are not translated.

fastapi.md — links to newsletter.md and fastapi-people.md#fastapi-experts, which are not translated.
This impacts all 12 locales that are translated (de, es, fr, hi, ja, ko, pt, ru, tr, uk, zh, zh-hant).

What I changed
Replaced broken relative links with absolute links to the English pages:

Old = ../release-notes.md
mew = https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/release-notes/

old = newsletter.md
new = https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/newsletter/

old = fastapi-people.md#fastapi-experts
new = ht

Why absolute URLs
These pages (release-notes, newsletter, fastapi-people) are only maintained in English. title: fix: use None sentinel instead of mutable OAuthFlowsModel() default in OAuth2.__init__
text:
## Summary

`OAuth2.__init__` uses `OAuthFlowsModel()` as a mutable default argument. Every call to `OAuth2()` without explicit `flows` shares the same `OAuthFlowsModel` instance. Mutations to that instance propagate across all default-using instances.

Changed to `None` sentinel with `if flows is None: flows = OAuthFlowsModel()` inside the function body.

## Verification
- Called whenever OAuth2 is instantiated without explicit flows.
- Consistent with how `SecurityScopes` (same file, line 666)

title: fix: pass include/exclude/by_alias params to jsonable_encoder when no response_model
text:
## Summary

`serialize_response` receives `include`, `exclude`, `by_alias`, `exclude_unset`, `exclude_defaults`, and `exclude_none` parameters. When `field` is None (no `response_model`), it calls `jsonable_encoder(response_content)` without passing any of those filtering parameters. They are silently ignored.

A user who writes `@app.get("/items", response_model_include={"name", "id"})` without a `response_model` would expect the exclude to work, but it doesn't.

## Verification
- Not dead code

text:

text:
Hi — thanks for FastAPI.

I noticed the published wheels lost their signed provenance in the switch to `uv`, and I don't think it was intended. Checking PyPI's integrity API:

| version | uploaded | `/integrity/.../provenance` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0.127.0 | 2025-12-21 | HTTP 200 — signed |
| 0.128.0 | 2025-12-27 | HTTP 200 — signed |
| **0.129.0** | 2026-02-12 | **HTTP 404 — none** |
| 0.139.0 (latest) | 2026-07-01 | HTTP 404 — none |

The first release without provenance is the first one aft

title: Restore PEP 740 release attestations (lost in the uv migration)
text:
(latest) | 2026-07-01 | HTTP 404 — none |

The first release without provenance is the first one after `⬆️ Migrate to uv (#14676)`. That commit replaced `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish` (which emits PEP 740 attestations by default for Trusted Publishing projects) with `uv publish`, and uv's docs note it *"does not currently generate attestations."* The Trusted Publishing identity (`id-token: write`) is still configured, so it looks like only the emission step was dropped, silently — nothing fails i

title: Restore PEP 740 release attestations (lost in the uv migration)
text:
is still configured, so it looks like only the emission step was dropped, silently — nothing fails in CI when attestations stop being produced, which is probably why it went unnoticed.

This PR keeps `uv build` and hands the upload back to `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish`, which restores attestation emission. It's the one step, nothing else changes.

For a quick sanity check that the action still attests under Trusted Publishing: `huggingface/transformers` publishes this way and its wheels carry pr

I may be missing a reason `uv publish` was preferred here — if so, please just close this, no problem at all. If you'd rather keep `uv publish` and generate the attestations separately before upload, that works too; happy to adjust.

title: 🐛 Fix race condition in _IncludedRouter cache rebuild under concurrent first requests
text:
Fixes #15974. Also reported in discussion #15914.

## Problem

`_IncludedRouter.effective_candidates()` and `_IncludedRouter.effective_low_priority_routes()` rebuild their cached lists lazily with no synchronization. The rebuild publishes an empty list on the shared attribute before filling it and stamps the version afterwards. When several threads send the app's first requests concurrently (per-thread `TestClient`s in a parallel test suite, or any setup that serves one app object from multiple

title: 🐛 Fix race condition in _IncludedRouter cache rebuild under concurrent first requests
text:
hread `TestClient`s in a parallel test suite, or any setup that serves one app object from multiple event loops), multiple threads pass the version check and append into the same list. The cache ends up permanently holding duplicated candidates (around 600 entries for a 120 route app in the repro), a concurrent reader can see a partially built list and 404 a valid route, and the interleaved `warnings.catch_warnings()` calls inside the rebuild can leak global warnings filters.

## Fix

Guard the

title: 🐛 Fix race condition in _IncludedRouter cache rebuild under concurrent first requests
text:
ngs.catch_warnings()` calls inside the rebuild can leak global warnings filters.

## Fix

Guard the rebuild with a per-instance lock and double-checked version test, build the new list into a local variable, and publish it atomically (list first, version second). Readers on the fast path never see a partial list, concurrent first requests trigger exactly one rebuild, and the warnings filter state is no longer touched by interleaved rebuilds of the same router.

The lock field is excluded from th

title: 🐛 Fix race condition in _IncludedRouter cache rebuild under concurrent first requests
text:
is no longer touched by interleaved rebuilds of the same router.

The lock field is excluded from the dataclass `repr` and `eq` so existing semantics are unchanged.

## Tests

Added `tests/test_included_router_concurrent_rebuild.py`, which fires the first requests from several threads through a barrier and asserts that all requests succeed and that the cache holds exactly one candidate per route. It fails on master and passes with this change. All existing router and include tests pass.

title: ⚡️ Optimize dependency graph flattening
text:
## Summary

Replace recursive dependency-graph flattening with an iterative preorder traversal.

The previous implementation constructed a flattened subtree at each dependency level and copied that subtree into every ancestor. It also used linear list membership when skipping repeated dependencies.

This change:

- accumulates dependencies directly into one flat result;
- uses set-backed repeated-dependency detection, while retaining compatibility with unhashable callables;
- replaces recursive

title: ⚡️ Optimize dependency graph flattening
⚡️ Optimize dependency graph flattening
text:
t dependency execution.

## Complexity

For a dependency chain of depth `d`, the previous recursive implementation repeatedly copied descendant lists into their ancestors, resulting in `O(d²)` work and memory references.

The iterative implementation traverses the dependency graph and accumulates the flattened result directly, making a chain `O(d)`.

For repeated dependencies, set-backed membership changes duplicate detection from `O(n²)` to average `O(n)` for hashable dependency cache keys. The

title: ⚡️ Optimize dependency graph flattening
text:
p changes duplicate detection from `O(n²)` to average `O(n)` for hashable dependency cache keys. The list fallback preserves support for unhashable callables.

## Internal representation

The root flattened `Dependant` retains the same preorder dependency sequence and combined parameter fields.

One internal detail changes: entries in the root flat dependency list no longer retain their own recursively flattened descendant lists. All descendants are accumulated directly in the root flat list. Ex

title: ⚡️ Optimize dependency graph flattening
text:
ively flattened descendant lists. All descendants are accumulated directly in the root flat list. Existing FastAPI consumers operate on the root flat collections.

## Benchmarks

A local synthetic benchmark flattening a 500-node dependency chain with `skip_repeats=True` measured:

| Implementation | Time |
|---|---:|
| `master` | ~7.8 ms |
| This PR | ~1.6 ms |

This is approximately a 4.9× improvement for that case.

The PR adds a focused CodSpeed benchmark so CI can provide the authoritative c

title: Fix SSE data payload dropping trailing newlines
text:
### Summary

`format_sse_event` splits the data payload with `str.splitlines()` before writing each `data:` field. This silently drops a **trailing** newline, so a `ServerSentEvent` whose data ends in `\n` is sent one field short and a client reconstructs the payload without its final newline.

`str.splitlines()` also treats characters as line breaks that the SSE wire format does **not** recognize (`\v`, `\f`, `\x1c`–`\x1e`, `\x85`, ` `, ` `), so those characters inside `raw_data` — documented a

title: Fix SSE data payload dropping trailing newlines
text:
(`\v`, `\f`, `\x1c`–`\x1e`, `\x85`, ` `, ` `), so those characters inside `raw_data` — documented as sent "as-is" — get wrongly split into separate `data:` fields.

### Reproduction

```python
from fastapi.sse import format_sse_event

format_sse_event(data_str="line1\n")
# actual:   b'data: line1\n\n'          -> client rebuilds "line1"  (trailing "\n" lost)
# expected: b'data: line1\ndata: \n\n'  -> client rebuilds "line1\n"

format_sse_event(data_str="a\x0bb")
# actual:   b'data: a\ndata: b\n

title: Fix SSE data payload dropping trailing newlines
text:
-> client rebuilds "line1
"

format_sse_event(data_str="a\x0bb")
# actual:   b'data: a
data: b

'     -> "\x0b" turned into a line break
# expected: b'data: a\x0bb

'         -> "\x0b" sent as-is
```

Per the [WHATWG event-stream format](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/server-sent-events.html#event-stream-interpretation), a stream is split into lines on **CR LF, CR, or LF only**, and a `data:` value is joined back with `
` on the client. To transmit `"line1
"` the server must em

title: Fix SSE data payload dropping trailing newlines
text:
d a `data:` value is joined back with `\n` on the client. To transmit `"line1\n"` the server must emit `data: line1` followed by an empty `data:` field.

### Fix

Split the payload on the SSE line terminators (`\r\n`, `\r`, `\n`) and keep the trailing empty field, instead of using `str.splitlines()`. Multi-line data, CR, and CRLF continue to encode exactly as before.

A unit test covering the trailing-newline, empty, multi-line, CR/CRLF, and non-SSE-separator cases is added. `fastapi/sse.py` sta

title: 🐛 Fix `exclude_defaults` not propagated to dict keys and values in `jsonable_encoder`
text:
## Problem

`jsonable_encoder` forwards `exclude_defaults` when recursing into list/tuple/set items, but drops it when recursing into dict keys and values — while the sibling flags `exclude_unset` and `exclude_none` *are* forwarded in that same dict branch. The same model with the same flag encodes differently depending on its container:

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel
from fastapi.encoders import jsonable_encoder

class M(BaseModel):
    a: int = 5

jsonable_encoder([M()], exclude_def

title: 🐛 Fix `exclude_defaults` not propagated to dict keys and values in `jsonable_encoder`
text:
ers import jsonable_encoder

class M(BaseModel):
    a: int = 5

jsonable_encoder([M()], exclude_defaults=True)       # [{}]
jsonable_encoder({"k": M()}, exclude_defaults=True)  # {"k": {"a": 5}}  <- flag silently ignored
```

Reproduced on 0.139.2.

## Fix

Forward `exclude_defaults` in the dict branch's key and value recursion, matching the list branch and the two sibling flags already passed there.

This deliberately does **not** change `include`/`exclude` propagation for dict values — that's

text:
ere.

This deliberately does **not** change `include`/`exclude` propagation for dict values — that's the broader design question tracked in discussion #15961; this PR only removes the inconsistency between the two container branches for a flag that is already documented as recursive.

## Tests

Added `test_encode_model_with_default_in_dict_and_list` covering list, dict, and dict-of-list nesting plus a guard that `exclude_unset`/`exclude_none` behaviour is unchanged.

title: 🐛 Fix `Form()` with an `Optional` Pydantic model silently discarding submitted data
text:
### Bug

A form body parameter typed as `Optional[SomeModel]` (`SomeModel | None`) silently drops the submitted fields and resolves to `None` with **no validation error** — while the equivalent JSON body parses correctly. Simply adding `| None` to an otherwise-working `Annotated[SomeModel, Form()]` parameter breaks it.

```python

title: Optimize APIRoute handler caching and fix endpoint context cache
text:
## Summary

This PR fixes two issues in `routing.py`:

1. Cache the generated request handler for effective route contexts to avoid rebuilding it on every request.
2. Replace the `id()`-based endpoint context cache with a `WeakKeyDictionary` to avoid stale cache entries and allow unused entries to be garbage-collected.

## Motivation

While reviewing `routing.py`, I noticed that routes using an effective route context rebuild their request handler on every incoming request, even though

title: Optimize APIRoute handler caching and fix endpoint context cache
text:
ing an effective route context rebuild their request handler on every incoming request, even though the effective context itself is already cached and stable. Caching the generated ASGI application avoids repeating the same work and reduces unnecessary allocations.

I also noticed that `_endpoint_context_cache` is keyed by `id(func)`. Since object IDs may be reused after an object is garbage-collected, this can theoretically return stale endpoint metadata. Additionally, the cache never shrinks

title: Optimize APIRoute handler caching and fix endpoint context cache
text:
lected, this can theoretically return stale endpoint metadata. Additionally, the cache never shrinks because entries remain for the lifetime of the process. Using `WeakKeyDictionary` avoids both issues.

## Changes

- Added lazy caching of the generated ASGI application on `_EffectiveRouteContext`.
- Reused the cached application for subsequent requests.
- Replaced the `id()`-based endpoint context cache with `weakref.WeakKeyDictionary`.
- Added a fallback for callables that cannot be wea

title: Optimize APIRoute handler caching and fix endpoint context cache
text:
context cache with `weakref.WeakKeyDictionary`.
- Added a fallback for callables that cannot be weak-referenced by computing the context without caching.

## Expected Impact

- Reduces repeated request handler construction.
- Avoids unnecessary allocations on repeated requests.
- Eliminates potential stale cache lookups caused by `id()` reuse.
- Prevents unbounded growth of the endpoint context cache.
- Preserves existing behavior while improving efficiency.

## Related Discussion

title: Optimize APIRoute handler caching and fix endpoint context cache
text:
ntext cache.
- Preserves existing behavior while improving efficiency.

## Related Discussion

Related to: #discussion-10445342

## Testing

- Added tests covering the new behavior.
- Verified that the existing test suite passes.
- Confirmed that routing behavior remains unchanged while exercising the modified code paths.

### Description

Hi 👋

I have been trying out the new `app.frontend()` helper to serve a single page app, using `fallback="index.html"` so that client side routes fall back to the shell and the frontend router can take over. This is the behavior described in the "Client side routing" part of the docs, and it works fine for a path like `/dashboard` or `/dashboard/settings`.

The problem shows up when a client side route has a dot in its l

shboard` or `/dashboard/settings`.

The problem shows up when a client side route has a dot in its last path segment. Plenty of real apps have these, for example a profile at `/users/john.doe`, a version deep link at `/v/1.2.3`, or a slug like `/files/report.2024`. When I open one of those directly, or just hit refresh while I am already on that page, I get a 404 instead of the `index.html` shell, so the app never loads and the client router never gets a chance to handle the route.

The part tha

so the app never loads and the client router never gets a chance to handle the route.

The part that surprised me is that setting `fallback="index.html"` explicitly does not change this. As far as I can tell there is currently no way to get these routes to fall back to the shell.

I spent some time reading the code and I think it comes from `_is_frontend_navigation_request()` in `fastapi/routing.py`. It takes the last path segment and if `os.path.splitext(...)` finds an extension it returns ear

py`. It takes the last path segment and if `os.path.splitext(...)` finds an extension it returns early and treats the request as an asset request, before it ever looks at the `Accept` header. Because `os.path.splitext("john.doe")` returns `.doe`, any segment with a dot in it is treated as a file and never gets the `index.html` fallback, even when the browser clearly asked for `text/html`.

What makes me think this is fixable without regressions is that the two situations are easy to tell apart.

title: fix: use None sentinel instead of mutable OAuthFlowsModel() default in OAuth2.__init__
text:
## Summary

`OAuth2.__init__` uses `OAuthFlowsModel()` as a mutable default argument. Every call to `OAuth2()` without explicit `flows` shares the same `OAuthFlowsModel` instance. Mutations to that instance propagate across all default-using instances.

Changed to `None` sentinel with `if flows is None: flows = OAuthFlowsModel()` inside the function body.

## Verification
- Called whenever OAuth2 is instantiated without explicit flows.
- Consistent with how `SecurityScopes` (same file, line 666)

title: fix: pass include/exclude/by_alias params to jsonable_encoder when no response_model
text:
## Summary

`serialize_response` receives `include`, `exclude`, `by_alias`, `exclude_unset`, `exclude_defaults`, and `exclude_none` parameters. When `field` is None (no `response_model`), it calls `jsonable_encoder(response_content)` without passing any of those filtering parameters. They are silently ignored.

A user who writes `@app.get("/items", response_model_include={"name", "id"})` without a `response_model` would expect the exclude to work, but it doesn't.

## Verification
- Not dead code

title: Restore PEP 740 release attestations (lost in the uv migration)
text:
Hi — thanks for FastAPI.

I noticed the published wheels lost their signed provenance in the switch to `uv`, and I don't think it was intended. Checking PyPI's integrity API:

| version | uploaded | `/integrity/.../provenance` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0.127.0 | 2025-12-21 | HTTP 200 — signed |
| 0.128.0 | 2025-12-27 | HTTP 200 — signed |
| **0.129.0** | 2026-02-12 | **HTTP 404 — none** |
| 0.139.0 (latest) | 2026-07-01 | HTTP 404 — none |

The first release without provenance is the first one aft

title: Restore PEP 740 release attestations (lost in the uv migration)
text:
(latest) | 2026-07-01 | HTTP 404 — none |

The first release without provenance is the first one after `⬆️ Migrate to uv (#14676)`. That commit replaced `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish` (which emits PEP 740 attestations by default for Trusted Publishing projects) with `uv publish`, and uv's docs note it *"does not currently generate attestations."* The Trusted Publishing identity (`id-token: write`) is still configured, so it looks like only the emission step was dropped, silently — nothing fails i

title: Restore PEP 740 release attestations (lost in the uv migration)
text:
is still configured, so it looks like only the emission step was dropped, silently — nothing fails in CI when attestations stop being produced, which is probably why it went unnoticed.

This PR keeps `uv build` and hands the upload back to `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish`, which restores attestation emission. It's the one step, nothing else changes.

For a quick sanity check that the action still attests under Trusted Publishing: `huggingface/transformers` publishes this way and its wheels carry pr

title: Restore PEP 740 release attestations (lost in the uv migration)
text:
ests under Trusted Publishing: `huggingface/transformers` publishes this way and its wheels carry provenance today (`https://pypi.org/integrity/transformers/5.13.1/transformers-5.13.1-py3-none-any.whl/provenance` → 200).

I may be missing a reason `uv publish` was preferred here — if so, please just close this, no problem at all. If you'd rather keep `uv publish` and generate the attestations separately before upload, that works too; happy to adjust.

title: 🐛 Fix race condition in _IncludedRouter cache rebuild under concurrent first requests
text:
Fixes #15974. Also reported in discussion #15914.

## Problem

`_IncludedRouter.effective_candidates()` and `_IncludedRouter.effective_low_priority_routes()` rebuild their cached lists lazily with no synchronization. The rebuild publishes an empty list on the shared attribute before filling it and stamps the version afterwards. When several threads send the app's first requests concurrently (per-thread `TestClient`s in a parallel test suite, or any setup that serves one app object from multiple

title: 🐛 Fix race condition in _IncludedRouter cache rebuild under concurrent first requests
text:
hread `TestClient`s in a parallel test suite, or any setup that serves one app object from multiple event loops), multiple threads pass the version check and append into the same list. The cache ends up permanently holding duplicated candidates (around 600 entries for a 120 route app in the repro), a concurrent reader can see a partially built list and 404 a valid route, and the interleaved `warnings.catch_warnings()` calls inside the rebuild can leak global warnings filters.

## Fix

Guard the

title: 🐛 Fix race condition in _IncludedRouter cache rebuild under concurrent first requests
text:
ngs.catch_warnings()` calls inside the rebuild can leak global warnings filters.

## Fix

Guard the rebuild with a per-instance lock and double-checked version test, build the new list into a local variable, and publish it atomically (list first, version second). Readers on the fast path never see a partial list, concurrent first requests trigger exactly one rebuild, and the warnings filter state is no longer touched by interleaved rebuilds of the same router.

The lock field is excluded from th

title: 🐛 Fix race condition in _IncludedRouter cache rebuild under concurrent first requests
text:
is no longer touched by interleaved rebuilds of the same router.

The lock field is excluded from the dataclass `repr` and `eq` so existing semantics are unchanged.

## Tests

Added `tests/test_included_router_concurrent_rebuild.py`, which fires the first requests from several threads through a barrier and asserts that all requests succeed and that the cache holds exactly one candidate per route. It fails on master and passes with this change. All existing router and include tests pass.

### Description

Since the router refactor in 0.137.0 (#15745), `_IncludedRouter.effective_candidates()` and `_IncludedRouter.effective_low_priority_routes()` in `fastapi/routing.py` rebuild their cached lists lazily on first use, with no synchronization.

The rebuild publishes an empty list on the shared attribute first, appends routes into it one by one, and only stamps the version at the end:

```python
self._effective_candidates = []
# ... appends into self._effective_candidates in a loop ..

```python
self._effective_candidates = []
# ... appends into self._effective_candidates in a loop ...
self._effective_candidates_version = routes_version
```

If several threads drive the app's first requests at the same time (for example per-thread `TestClient`s in a parallel test suite, or any embedding that serves one app object from multiple event loops), more than one thread can pass the version check and rebuild concurrently. Every rebuilder appends into whichever list was assigned to the

title: Race condition in _IncludedRouter cache rebuild can 404 valid routes and permanently corrupt the candidate cache
text:
ion check and rebuild concurrently. Every rebuilder appends into whichever list was assigned to the attribute last, so the cache ends up with duplicated candidates, and the corruption is permanent because the version gets stamped anyway. A request that runs while the list is still partially built can also get a 404 for a route that exists.

The rebuild path additionally uses `warnings.catch_warnings()` internally (via response field construction), so interleaved rebuilds can leak entries into th

### Expected behavior

The cache rebuild should be thread safe. Building the list into a local variable and publishing it atomically (list first, version second) keep
